q-34381.name: Question 1
q-34381.problem: What is the curvature of the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{2},{t}^{3}⟩$, for $t>0?$
q-34381.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})⟩=⟨2t,3{t}^{2}⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(2t)^{2}+(3{t}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+9{t}^{4}} \\  & =t\sqrt{4+9{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that since $t>0$, we have $|t|=t.$

Now, we find the second derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2})⟩=⟨2,6t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${r}^{″}(t)$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t) & =⟨2t,\,3{t}^{2},\,0⟩\times ⟨2,\,6t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2t & 3{t}^{2} & 0 \\ 2 & 6t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}2t & 3{t}^{2} \\ 2 & 6t\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =6{t}^{2}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

So, the magnitude of the cross product is

$$
‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖=6{t}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{6{t}^{2}}{(t\sqrt{4+9{t}^{2}})^{3}} \\  & =\frac{6{t}^{2}}{{t}^{3}(4+9{t}^{2})^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{6}{t(4+9{t}^{2})^{3/2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

What is the curvature of the curve r(t)=⟨t2,t3⟩, for t>0?

a
6t2(4+9t2)3/2
b
6t(4+9t2)3/2
c
18t(4+9t2)3/2
d
6t(4+9t2)3/2
e
6t(4+9t2)1/2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The curvature κ is given by κ(t)=‖r′(t)×r″(t)‖‖r′(t)‖3.

First, we calculate r′(t) and ‖r′(t)‖:

r′(t)=⟨ddt(t2),ddt(t3)⟩=⟨2t,3t2⟩‖r′(t)‖=(2t)2+(3t2)2=4t2+9t4=t4+9t2

Notice that since t>0, we have |t|=t.

Now, we find the second derivative:

r″(t)=⟨ddt(2t),ddt(3t2)⟩=⟨2,6t⟩

Next, we compute the cross product by considering r′(t) and r″(t) as 3-dimensional vectors with zero z-components:

r′(t)×r″(t)=⟨2t,3t2,0⟩×⟨2,6t,0⟩=ijk2t3t2026t0=2t3t226tk=6t2k

So, the magnitude of the cross product is ‖r′(t)×r″(t)‖=6t2.

Therefore, the curvature is

κ(t)=‖r′(t)×r″(t)‖‖r′(t)‖3=6t2(t4+9t2)3=6t2t3(4+9t2)3/2=6t(4+9t2)3/2.

q-83403.name: Question 2
q-83403.problem:
Given the curve $r(t)=⟨3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,4t⟩,$ use the cross product curvature formula to find the curvature of this curve as a function of $t.$ 

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)=12\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-12\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j-9k.$*
q-83403.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(t)$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,4⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{cos}^{2}⁡t+9{sin}^{2}⁡t+16} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Since we are told that

$$
{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)=12\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-12\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j-9k,
$$

we have

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(12\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-12\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-9)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{144+81} \\  & =15\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{15}{{5}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{3}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given the curve r(t)=⟨3sin⁡t,3cos⁡t,4t⟩, use the cross product curvature formula to find the curvature of this curve as a function of t.

Hint: You can use the fact that r′(t)×r″(t)=12cos⁡ti−12sin⁡tj−9k.

EXPLANATION

The curvature κ(t) is given by

κ(t)=‖r′(t)×r″(t)‖‖r′(t)‖3.

First, we calculate r′(t) and ‖r′(t)‖:

r′(t)=⟨ddt(3sin⁡t),ddt(3cos⁡t),ddt(4t)⟩=⟨3cos⁡t,−3sin⁡t,4⟩‖r′(t)‖=(3cos⁡t)2+(−3sin⁡t)2+42=9cos2⁡t+9sin2⁡t+16=25=5

Since we are told that

r′(t)×r″(t)=12cos⁡ti−12sin⁡tj−9k,

we have

‖r′(t)×r″(t)‖=(12cos⁡t)2+(−12sin⁡t)2+(−9)2=144+81=15 Therefore, the curvature is

κ(t)=‖r′(t)×r″(t)‖‖r′(t)‖3=1553=325.

q-86799.name: Question 3
q-86799.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨-t,\,4,\,1+\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩$ for $0\le t\le \pi $, use the cross product curvature formula to find the curvature as a function of $t.$
q-86799.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(t)$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩=⟨-1,\,0,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}+(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡(t)}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the second derivative ${r}^{″}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩=⟨0,\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the cross-product:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t) & =⟨-1,0,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\times ⟨0,0,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & 0 & \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 0 & 0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}-1 & \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|k \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the magnitude of the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖ & =|\operatorname{sin}⁡t|=\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $\operatorname{sin}⁡t\ge 0$ when $0\le t\le \pi .$

Therefore, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{(1+{cos}^{2}⁡(t))^{3/2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-132014.name: Question 4
q-132014.problem: Using the cross product curvature formula, find the curvature of $r(t)=⟨t,\,{e}^{-t}⟩$ as a function of $t.$
q-132014.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-{e}^{-t}⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-{e}^{-t})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{e}^{-2t}+1} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}}{{e}^{t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the second derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{-t})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,{e}^{-t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${r}^{″}(t)$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t) & =⟨1,\,-{e}^{-t},\,0⟩\times ⟨0,\,{e}^{-t},\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -{e}^{-t} & 0 \\ 0 & {e}^{-t} & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}1 & -{e}^{-t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & ={e}^{-t}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

So, the magnitude of the cross product is

$$
‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖={e}^{-t}.
$$

Therefore, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{-t}}{{(\frac{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}}{{e}^{t}})}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{-t}}{(\frac{\sqrt{{({e}^{2t}+1)}^{3}}}{{e}^{3t}})} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2t}}{\sqrt{{({e}^{2t}+1)}^{3}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-132051.problem: Using the cross product curvature formula, find the curvature of $r(t)=⟨4{t}^{2},\,4t⟩$ as a function of $t.$
q-132051.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t)⟩ \\  & =⟨8t,\,4⟩ \\  & =4⟨2t,\,1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =4\sqrt{(2t)^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =4\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the second derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =4⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =4⟨2,\,0⟩ \\  & =8⟨1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${r}^{″}(t)$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t) & =(4⟨2t,\,1,\,0⟩)\times (8⟨1,\,0,\,0⟩) \\  & =32\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2t & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =32\,\left|\begin{aligned}2t & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =-32\,k\end{aligned}
$$

So, the magnitude of the cross product is

$$
‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖=32.
$$

Therefore, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{32}{{(4\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+1})}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{32}{64\sqrt{{(4{t}^{2}+1)}^{3}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{(4{t}^{2}+1)}^{3}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Using the cross product curvature formula, find the curvature of r(t)=⟨4t2,4t⟩ as a function of t.

a
14t2+1
b
2(4t2+1)3
c
12(4t2+1)3
d
1(4t2+1)3
e
2(4t2+1)2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The curvature κ is given by κ(t)=‖r′(t)×r″(t)‖‖r′(t)‖3.

First, we calculate r′(t) and ‖r′(t)‖: r′(t)=⟨ddt(4t2),ddt(4t)⟩=⟨8t,4⟩=4⟨2t,1⟩‖r′(t)‖=4(2t)2+12=44t2+1

Now, we find the second derivative: r″(t)=4⟨ddt(2t),ddt(1)⟩=4⟨2,0⟩=8⟨1,0⟩

Next, we compute the cross product by considering r′(t) and r″(t) as 3-dimensional vectors with zero z-components: r′(t)×r″(t)=(4⟨2t,1,0⟩)×(8⟨1,0,0⟩)=32ijk2t10100=322t110k=−32k

So, the magnitude of the cross product is ‖r′(t)×r″(t)‖=32.

Therefore, the curvature is κ(t)=‖r′(t)×r″(t)‖‖r′(t)‖3=32(44t2+1)3=3264(4t2+1)3=12(4t2+1)3.
